title: Merge entropy scratchpad: dependency chain & rollback heuristics
content:
Problem statement:
- Observed a cluster of flaky failures after a batch of dependency bumps (protobuf, onnx, and a minor runtime change). Failures are nondeterministic and often only surface in the nightly pipeline.
- Hypothesis: a transitive change (serialization order or default rounding) + cache warmup timing interacts with our continuous batching path, creating rare state that fails assertions.

High-level goal:
- Reduce merge "entropy": the combinatorial surprise when multiple small changes interact in non-linear ways.
- Create a lightweight checklist and rollback-safe tactics to use when a PR touches dependencies or call graph boundaries.

Quick decision rubric (0-5 risk score; >=3 => more caution)
- Touches transitive deps with native bindings (numpy/protobuf/etc): +2
- Touches RPC/serialization code or stable on-disk formats: +2
- Changes runtime-critical hotpath (kv cache, batching): +2
- Increases concurrency/callbacks/async usage in runtime: +1
- No new tests around the affected code paths: +1

Recommended review checklist for dependency or boundary PRs:
- Does the PR include a short, reproducible local repro (unit or small integration)? If not, request one.
- Run the PR branch against A) unit tests B) small integration harness C) nightly-like load (simulate concurrency). Note any flakiness.
- Check presubmits for nondeterministic test markers ("flaky"/"unstable"). If tests were skipped historically, get context.
- Validate serialization compat: run schema round-trip tests (serialize -> deserialize) for representative payloads.
- Audit native/native-binding version matrix: are there platform-specific (glibc, macos) behaviors?
- Confirm pinned transitive deps in deployment manifests (docker layer): ensure rollout uses intended artifact.

Fast mitigations when rollouts show noise:
- Canary with traffic-shedding: route 5-10% traffic to the new binary and keep a short retention window for logs.
- Auto-fallback: use model-routing fallback to a compatible variant if latency/error rate exceeds threshold.
- Revert strategy: prefer a two-step revert: A) disable feature flags / route away, B) revert commit if A fails.

Investigation notes (what I ran locally):
- Reproduced failure only when running 8 concurrent request generators + cache warmup enabled. 2 generators or cache disabled=>no fail.
- Stack traces point to rounding inside packed buffer write (protobuf field ordering differs when map insertion order changes).
- Hypothesis: an assumption in runtime about deterministic map order is violated by updated protobuf/native combination.

Experiment plan (next 72h):
- Add a deterministic-map-wrapper in the serialization shim for the hotpath; run 1000 short runs across x86/arm images.
- Add additional unit that asserts canonical ordering for representative payloads.
- If deterministic wrapper reduces failures, track perf impact (latency p99 delta). If >5ms p99, explore keyed pre-sort approach only for fields that matter.

Follow-ups for PR hygiene (notes-to-self):
- Encourage PR authors to include a "system-level smoke test" section in PR template when bumping native deps. Add example commands.
- Add a small CI job: "dependency-smoke-8concurrency" that runs nightly for any merge touching python-native wheel builds.
- Create a short doc in Confluence describing the merge-entropy rubric and link to it from PR template.

Communication snippets (to post on PR or Slack):
- "Heads up: this change touches serialization native bindings. Before merging, can you add a small repro and run the 8-concurrency smoke harness? See linked infra job for commands."
- "If we see nondeterministic failures after merge, prefer routing away traffic and rolling back the artifact rather than immediate repo revert — gives us time to capture traces."

Quick checklist for an immediate rollback (if nightly spikes):
- Check current deploy artifact id for the host pool and pin traffic back to previous image.
- Capture logs + stack samples for 15min window.
- Open a triage ticket with tags: incident, regression, dependency. Assign to oncall + author.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there other map-like structures we assume to be ordered? (KV cache indexing? routing table iteration?)
- Can we add deterministic serialization at the protobuf layer without perf hit across all payload sizes?
- Is our canary traffic fraction and duration adequate? (current default: 5% for 30m)

Random heuristics / heuristics I keep forgetting:
- When in doubt, add a small unit test that asserts canonical bytes for a few representative payloads — cheap and catches a lot.
- Prefer feature flags for behavioral changes rather than large dependency rollouts. Easier to toggle.

TODO / next actions (me / tomorrow):
- [ ] Implement deterministic-map-wrapper in runtime serialization shim (branch: rylan/deterministic-serialize).
- [ ] Add canonical-serialization unit tests + CI gating.
- [ ] Create dependency-smoke CI job ticket (INF-XXXXX) and link in PR template.
- [ ] Post summary to #eng-serving-runtime with findings and recommended checklist.

Notes to self: keep this doc short — once we have a small postmortem, promote steps to a living Confluence checklist and replace ad-hoc notes here.

End of scratchpad.
